title: Utah scores win against Kalshi as company halts operations in state | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Utah prosecutors dropped criminal charges against the prediction company Kalshi and its co-founders on Tuesday, one day after the company halted operations in the state.

This is the latest — and perhaps most dramatic — victory for the states in their longstanding push to regulate prediction marketslike gambling. The companies and theTrump administrationinsist they should be federally regulated as financial exchanges.

Prediction platforms let users bet on real-world events, like sports,elections, the weather and more. Kalshi is the biggest prediction market in the US, but some or all of its markets are now unavailable in Utah,Nevada, Michigan,Louisianaand Washington state after the states fought back against the companies.

Utah Attorney General Derek Brown, a Republican, pursued bothcivil and criminal cases against Kalshi, ratcheting up the pressure. A conservative state with a sizable Mormon population, Utah has some of the strictest anti-gambling laws in the US, including a prohibition in itsstate constitution.

“Utah does not allow gambling, and prediction markets are gambling,” Brown said in a statement. “Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges. Every company in this space should take note. If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.”

There wasn’t any deal or settlement between Utah and Kalshi, according to two sources familiar with the matter. Kalshi unilaterally exited Utah on Monday after a setback in federal court, and state prosecutors asked the judge to dismiss the criminal case on Tuesday. Civil litigation is still pending.

Kalshi’s newly minted general counsel, former Trump-era Justice Department official Yaakov Roth,posted on Xthat he was “pleased” that Utah prosecutors dropped the criminal case and said the company is “ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.”

If the charges weren’t dropped, Kalshi co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Larawould berequired to appear in a Salt Lake City courtroom next week for theirarraignment.

Kalshi spokeswoman Jacki McGavick said in a statement that the company withdrew from Utah because of recent setbacks in federal court. A federal judge ruled months ago that Utah could enforce its gambling laws against Kalshi, and last week, the judge also largely rebuffed a new push by the Trump administration to shut down the state criminal case.

“This is an unfortunate outcome for the more than 177,000 Utahns who use Kalshi,” McGavick said. “We will continue to fight this in court, and we look forward to returning to Utah once our legal position is vindicated.”

The Utah case is one of dozens of lawsuits playing out across the country involving prediction markets like Kalshi andPolymarket, which have exploded in popularity this year and now see billions of dollars in weekly trading volume.

Experts believe the Supreme Court will ultimately decide the legality of prediction markets and who gets to regulate them. The states have seen significant momentum in recent months, withcourtroom victoriesand evenrecent actionon Capitol Hill.

States have argued that more regulations and consumer protections are needed because prediction markets are addictive like gambling and most users lose money.

However, it hasn’t been all bad news for the companies. A New York judge on Mondayrefusedto immediately shut down Kalshi in the state. But the developments in Utah show how a state can successfully pressure the companies with aggressive moves in state and federal court.

“Kalshi has steadfastly argued that it is legal under federal law and state laws don’t apply,” said Dustin Gouker, an independent journalist whochroniclesthe prediction industry. “But the threat of criminal charges against its co-founders has changed the calculus in terms of how far it’s willing to go to defend that argument.”

CNN has a partnership with Kalshi and uses its data to cover major events. CNN employees aren’t permitted to trade on prediction platforms.
